# Site audit

> Latest findings from `/iterate audit` and `/oversight`. Open
> items live here until a shipping skill drains them.

> **Rule 1: sliding window (locked 2026-05-14 — see `plan/bearings.md`
> § Rule 1).** Each pillar carries ≥2 articles published within the
> last 30 days, always. The rule is self-replenishing — articles
> aging out generate new shortfalls without any external priming.
>
> Three states, codified in bearings.md and emitted by the audit-row
> generator (phase 30 ships `scripts/content-gap-survey.mjs`):
>
> - **Comfortable** — every pillar ≥ 2 in 30d. No Rule-1 row files.
> - **Hot pursuit** — one or more pillars at exactly 1 in 30d. Row
>   files at score **7.0** for that pillar. Loop ships on next tick.
> - **Critical hot pursuit** — one or more pillars at 0 in 30d. Row
>   files at score **9.5**, above every other priority. Loop drops
>   iterate / polish until the pillar recovers.
>
> Pillar selection when multiple are cold: oldest most-recent
> publishedAt wins; tie-breaker is lowest count, then editorial
> prominence (Trends > News > Ideas > Deep Dives > Guides).
>
> **Current state (2026-05-14):** all 40 articles aged 1–10 days,
> all pillars at 8 in 30d → comfortable. First natural shortfall
> arrives in ~20 days as the oldest articles cross the threshold.
> No Rule-1 row to file yet.
>
> Rules 2 / 3 / 4 (tracker linkage, group-buy companion, publishedAt
> gap-fill) are unchanged. They compete on raw `impact × ease`.

> **PRUNE 2026-06-14 (via `/oversight`):** the 65 open
> `[cross-links] [3.6]` *adjacent-pillar* rows were deleted in bulk.
> Rationale: these were the weakest cross-link signal (adjacent
> pillar, ≥2 shared tags) and were draining 1/tick — ~58% of recent
> maintenance bandwidth went to them. The 52 stronger
> `[cross-links] [4.5]` *same-pillar* rows are kept; phase 46
> (cross-link drain efficiency) makes `/iterate` cluster-aware so
> those drain per-article instead of 1/tick. Phase 39's
> `article-crosslink-survey` will re-file adjacent-pillar pairs on
> the empty-queue path; if the drain re-dominates, raise the
> survey's adjacent-pillar floor rather than re-pruning by hand.

> **POSTURE: drained 2026-05-09** — the brand-assets-first
> posture set at 12:30Z is cleared. All four drain items shipped
> the same day: (1) favicon — `apps/web/src/app/icon.svg` +
> `apple-icon.tsx` wired via Next App Router auto-discovery
> (`0e7c9fd`); (2) default OG — already in place at
> `apps/web/src/app/opengraph-image.tsx` since phase 4 (`fc1b0b0`);
> (3) per-pillar OG variants — five `apps/web/src/app/<pillar>/opengraph-image.tsx`
> handlers + shared `<PillarOGContent>` template (`0dab0a8`);
> (4) hero placeholders for the six seed articles — SVGs at
> `apps/web/public/hero-art/<slug>.svg` + provenance JSON siblings
> + frontmatter `heroImage`/`heroImageAlt` wiring (`0e7c9fd`).
> `/march` resumes normal dispatch — phase 15 (Newsletter) is the
> next pending phase.

> **Iterate-bias category: cleared 2026-05-09** along with the
> posture. Iterate scoring returns to category-neutral.

> **Article hero art directive (locked 2026-05-09 — durable
> after the posture drained):** every article (current and future)
> renders a colorful keyboard SVG as its hero placeholder until
> real photography backfills. Style: simple, single splash of
> color, line-drawing weight consistent across articles,
> illustrative of the article's subject (switch cross-section
> for switch-deep-dives, keycap profile silhouette for keycap
> pieces, keyboard outline + callout for build pieces, sparkline
> for trends pieces, layout silhouette for ergonomic pieces).
> Hero SVGs land under `apps/web/public/hero-art/<slug>.svg` with
> a sibling `<slug>.svg.json` provenance file. The article
> frontmatter `heroImage` field references the absolute path.
>
> **Forward-looking wiring (added 2026-05-09 same drain):** new
> articles drafted by `/iterate` no longer ship art-less. The
> iterate skill's content-gap delegation now bundles
> `content-curator` (prose) + `brander` (hero SVG) + frontmatter
> wiring as a single commit — see `skills/iterate.md` § Step 3.
> The audit's "articles missing `heroImage`" finding (§4.A) is
> reserved for backfilling already-shipped articles, not for
> letting new ones slip through. Non-article asset findings
> (broken favicon, missing OG variant, stale render) still go
> through `/ship-asset` directly — that lane stays demand-pull
> per `skills/ship-asset.md` §1.

### [x] [engineering] [5.4] content-gap-survey.mjs missing isMain guard — its own 17 unit tests silently never ran — addressed in this commit, closes #783
- category: engineering
- filed: 2026-08-08 by cloud /iterate audit (fresh general-purpose sweep, angle: recently-touched scripts/*.mjs for regressions)
- impact: 6 (not user-facing, but it's the autonomous loop's own content-gap audit pipeline — every other `scripts/*.mjs` file with a `__test` export uses the `isMain` guard pattern; this one didn't, so its dedup logic added just hours earlier in commit 99a0fe89 shipped with zero real regression protection despite green CI)
- ease: 9 (one-line-pattern fix, already proven correct by the sibling `scripts/newsletter-gap-survey.mjs`)
- score: 5.4 (impact × ease / 10)
- observation: `scripts/content-gap-survey.mjs`'s CLI body ran unconditionally at module-eval time and ended with `process.exit(0)`. `scripts/__tests__/content-gap-survey.test.mjs` imports `__test` from the module as its first statement — ES module evaluation runs the imported module's top level first, so the import executed the full survey and called `process.exit(0)` before any of the file's 17 `test()`/`describe()` cases ever ran. The file collapsed to one opaque "ok" in `node --test` output instead of the 7 nested `describe()` subtests every sibling script shows.
- evidence: `grep -n "isMain" scripts/content-gap-survey.mjs scripts/newsletter-gap-survey.mjs` — 0 matches in content-gap-survey.mjs, 2 in newsletter-gap-survey.mjs. `node --test scripts/__tests__/content-gap-survey.test.mjs` before the fix showed a single collapsed "ok" with no nested subtests; after the fix, 17/17 tests pass across 7 suites.
- issue: #783
> **Resolved (2026-08-08):** moved the `__test` export above the CLI section and wrapped the CLI body (args parsing, article read, survey, write/dry-run branches, all `process.exit()` calls) in `const isMain = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === process.argv[1]` / `if (!isMain) { ... } else { ... }`, mirroring `scripts/newsletter-gap-survey.mjs` exactly. Verified `node --test scripts/__tests__/content-gap-survey.test.mjs` now runs and passes all 17 real subtests, and the CLI itself (`node scripts/content-gap-survey.mjs` / `--json`) still behaves identically.

- ease: 8 (one-file change to `.github/workflows/lighthouse.yml` — swap the audited base URL; no app/package code)
- score: 4.8 (impact × ease / 10)
- root cause: `.github/workflows/lighthouse.yml` sets `urls:` from `${{ github.event.deployment_status.target_url }}`, which is Vercel's immutable per-deployment hostname (e.g. `https://thock-hig8pokji-funkycoffee.vercel.app`). That hostname has Vercel Deployment Protection (Authentication / SSO) enabled, so Lighthouse follows a 307 to `https://vercel.com/login?next=…` and audits Vercel's login page — which fails `categories.accessibility`, `categories.best-practices`, `categories.seo`, `color-contrast`, and ~12 other assertions. The page under test is never thock.
- evidence: run 26217540757 (2026-05-21T09:26Z) and every prior run — `##[error]21 results for https://vercel.com/login?next=%2Fsso-api%3Furl%3D…thock-hig8pokji-funkycoffee.vercel.app…`. The `march` workflow and `pnpm deploy:check` are unaffected and green — this is isolated to the Lighthouse workflow.
- why the loop was blind to it: `/iterate` audit and `/march` read Vercel `deploy:check` + `plan/AUDIT.md` / `CRITIQUE.md` only; a failing non-`march` GitHub Actions workflow is invisible to autonomous ticks. This row is the bridge — without it the workflow stays red indefinitely.
- action: change `lighthouse.yml` `urls:` to audit the public production alias `https://thock.xyz` (the canonical `siteConfig.siteUrl`, not SSO-protected) instead of `target_url` — hardcode the four paths (`/`, `/article/gateron-oil-king-deep-dive`, `/trends/tracker`, `/group-buys`) against that base. Keep the `deployment_status` Production-success trigger as the run signal; only the audited URL changes. Fallback host `thock-coral.vercel.app` also resolves public if `thock.xyz` is unsuitable. (Alternative: disable Vercel Deployment Protection for the project — an out-of-repo dashboard setting; the canonical-alias fix is in-repo and preferred.)
- once fixed: the run page should show real category scores. If the genuine site then fails an assertion, that is a separate, real audit row.
- issue: #165
- blocker: cloud loop cannot push `.github/workflows/` files — ACTIONS_PAT needs `workflow` scope (classic PAT) or `workflows: write` permission (fine-grained). The fix is one line in lighthouse.yml (confirmed correct; soft-reset after push rejected on 2026-05-21 cloud tick). Drain requires a local push or ACTIONS_PAT scope upgrade.

### [x] [LOW] /sources per-citation index — phase 16 follow-up — addressed in e18e10b4b5c2476f6f020301297bb6f8fe3389e7 (this tick)
- issue: #19
> Filed 2026-05-09 by phase 16 brief. The /sources page currently surfaces the per-article aggregate count of `<Source>` tags. The full per-citation index (article → quote → URL) requires an MDX walker that parses every body, extracts each `<Source href= text= />` tuple, dedupes by href, and surfaces (article, quote, source) rows. Worth shipping but not phase-16 scope.
>
> **Action:** new helper `extractSourceCitations(body: string): Array<{ href, text, position }>` in `@thock/content/util/`; new section on `/sources` rendering the deduped citation list. Probably wants its own ship-data flow if the citation count grows large.
>
> Score: **3.5** (real but cosmetic with the current article count of 6).
>
> **Resolved (2026-05-10):** Shipped exactly the row's recommended action. Added `extractSourceCitations(body): SourceCitation[]` next to `countSourceTags` in `packages/content/src/util/sources.ts` — single regex matches both `<Source href="..." />` (self-closing) and `<Source href="...">text</Source>` (paired) forms, captures href + inner text + character offset; whitespace-collapses and trims the text content; skips tags missing an href attribute. Exported via `packages/content/src/index.ts`. Built `<CitationIndex>` + `buildCitationIndex` helper at `apps/web/src/components/sources/CitationIndex.tsx` that takes `(article, citation)` pairs, dedupes by href, sorts citing articles by publishedAt-desc per row, and sorts the final index by most-recent-citing-article. `/sources` page now renders the per-article tally first, then a "Citation index" section with the deduped per-citation list. Each row links to the external URL (with `rel="noopener" target="_blank"`), shows the host+path, and lists the citing articles. Mobile-safe: `break-all` on the host span and `break-words` on title links handle long URLs without horizontal overflow at 375px. New e2e in `apps/e2e/tests/polish.spec.ts` asserts the index renders with at least one row pointing at a real https URL. New unit tests in `packages/content/src/__tests__/util/sources.test.ts` cover the extractor's empty / paired / self-closing / order / whitespace-collapse / multi-line-attrs / missing-href edge cases. Article count is now 12 (not the 6 the audit row's score basis assumed); the catalog has 15 total citations across 12 articles, so the index is non-trivial. 325 e2e green serially; first parallel attempt hit two #418 flakes on / and /news (same root cause as expand pass-2 candidate).

### [x] [MED] [a11y] /trends/tracker — heading level skipped (h1 → h3 with no h2) — addressed in f70b1f3 (closes #33)
> Filed 2026-05-10 by /iterate audit pass (resolves the [MED] Accessibility audit pass row above).
>
> **Observation:** /trends/tracker's heading sequence is `h1 h3 h3 h3 h3 h2 h2 h2 h2 h2`. The h1 "What's actually rising this week" (offset 10804 in rendered HTML) is followed directly by four h3 cards ("Gateron Oil King", "Cherry MX2A revisions", "HMX Cloud", "Wuque Studio") at offsets 11947–15171, then later switch/keycap/layout/vendor/brand "movers" h2 sections. The h3-after-h1-without-h2 is a heading-level skip — screen-reader users navigating by heading jumps will perceive the rising cards as belonging to a missing or implied h2 section.
>
> **WCAG:** 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (AA).
>
> **Action:** likely the cleanest fix is to wrap the four "rising this week" card titles under a real h2 sub-section heading (e.g. an h2 "Top movers this week" right after the h1) so the structure becomes `h1 → h2 → h3*4 → h2*5`. Alternative: promote the four card titles from h3 to h2, joining the existing five movers h2 sections — but that loses the visual subordination of "preview cards" vs "category tables." Probably the wrap-with-h2 path is right; component is `apps/web/src/components/tracker/<RisingThisWeek?>` (search the codebase to find the actual file).
>
> Score: **4.0** (impact 5 — single page, real but narrow audience of heading-nav screen-reader users; ease 8 — one component edit + one e2e to lock the order).
>
> **Resolved (2026-05-10):** wrapped `<TrackerSummaryGrid>` in `apps/web/src/app/trends/tracker/page.tsx` with a visible h2 "This week at a glance" right after the TrackerHeader's h1. Sequence is now `h1 → h2 → h3*4 → h2*5` (no skip). Wording chosen over the audit's suggested "Top movers this week" because the four cards include Sleeper (which is flat by design — see also pending [MED] critique #8) — "movers" framing dilutes the Sleeper kind. New e2e regression guard at `apps/e2e/tests/trends.spec.ts` walks every heading in document order and asserts no level jump > 1 going down — catches future skips automatically. Verify: 409 e2e green parallel (no #418 flake this run).

- action: scoped fix — in `/about`'s body component, apply `underline` to inline prose links, OR add a `prose-a:underline` helper class on the prose wrapper. Do NOT remove `text-decoration: none` globally (other link contexts like nav, card titles, etc. rely on it). Targeted scope: `apps/web/src/components/about/AboutBody.tsx`.

- once fixed: add link-in-text-block assertion to a11y.spec.ts for /about

The Tailwind utility overrides the global `a { text-decoration: none }` baseline. Subtle accent underline at 40% opacity + bumps to full accent on hover keeps the editorial restraint while restoring the non-color affordance. ### [x] [engineering] [3.0] Tracked generated manifests are not build-portable — a local win32 build rewrites them wholesale — addressed in 94f4bbe, closes #382
- category: engineering
- filed: 2026-07-03 by the nexus readopt pass (local session)
- impact: 5 (manifest.generated.json / og-manifest.generated.json / index.generated.json are tracked but regenerated by `pnpm build`; the generator embeds the absolute build-machine `filePath` — `/home/runner/work/thock/...` from CI, `Z:\keyboard\...` locally — and preserves the source file's line endings inside JSON body strings, so a Windows build bakes `\r\n` into every article body. Any local build on win32 dirties three tracked files with machine-specific churn; a careless `git add -A` commits it, and the next CI build flips it all back)
- ease: 6 (make generation portable: store `filePath` repo-relative with posix separators; normalize body strings to LF at read time. Alternatively untrack the three files if nothing reads them from the repo at rest)
- score: 3.0 (impact × ease / 10)
- issue: #382
> **Resolved (2026-07-03):** `@thock/content`'s `readUtf8()` now normalizes CRLF → LF at read time; new `toRepoRelativePosix()` gives `filePath` a stable, repo-relative, posix-separated form used by both `articles.ts` and `newsletters.ts`. Both generator scripts (`generate-data-manifest.mts`, `generate-search-index.mts`) consume these loaders unchanged, so the fix propagates without touching the generators. All three generated files regenerated and committed in the same tick. `94f4bbe`.

### [blocked-cloud-permission] [engineering] [6.3] march.yml crash-issue gate never fires when the action itself fails — implicit `success()` swallows the one case it exists for
- category: engineering
- filed: 2026-07-05 by /iterate audit (cloud march tick)
- impact: 7 (the two steps exist specifically to surface a crashed cloud tick — "Upload Claude execution transcript" and "Open GitHub issue for problematic execution" — but both `if:` conditions at `.github/workflows/march.yml:240` and `:249` reference only `steps.inspect.outputs.has_issues`, with no `always()`/`failure()`/`cancelled()` term; GitHub Actions prepends an implicit `success()` to any custom condition lacking one of those three, so once the prior `claude_run` step fails the job's running status is already non-`success()` and both steps skip regardless of `has_issues` — exactly backwards, since the crash-before-transcript branch is the first case the inspect step's own logic handles. Confirmed via a direct reproduction: run `28721452962` (2026-07-04T22:19:29Z, `conclusion: failure`) shows the inspect step correctly logging `has_issues=true`/`has_transcript=false`, yet the issue-open step shows `conclusion: skipped` in the same job — no crash issue exists for that run)
- ease: 9 (two-line workflow-file change — add `always() &&` to the two `if:` conditions, mirroring the `always()` already present on the inspect step one step earlier; no route/schema/component/skill-file contract touched)
- score: 6.3 (impact × ease / 10)
- next: add `always() &&` to `.github/workflows/march.yml` steps 11 and 12's `if:` conditions
- issue: #395
- **blocked (this tick):** wrote the two-line fix, ran it through the full verify gate (green: typecheck, 591 web unit tests, data:validate, build, 959/959 e2e), committed locally, then `git push origin main` was rejected — `refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow ".github/workflows/march.yml" without "workflows" permission`. The push credential in cloud (a `ghs_`-prefixed GitHub App installation token, confirmed identical between `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` env vars in this session) lacks the `workflows` scope regardless of the `ACTIONS_PAT` secret the workflow's env block names for `gh` CLI calls — GitHub enforces this permission specifically on any push touching `.github/workflows/*`, and no PAT/App token scope currently granted to the cloud loop satisfies it. Reverted the local commit (`git reset --soft` + `git checkout HEAD --`) rather than leave an unpushed commit or push-fail-loop. **This is a standing cloud-loop constraint, not specific to this fix**: no future cloud tick can edit `.github/workflows/*.yml` until either the PAT backing `ACTIONS_PAT` is granted "Workflows: write" (fine-grained PAT permission) and wired as the git push credential (not just the `gh` CLI credential), or workflow-file changes are treated as local/`/oversight`-only edits (like brand-setup taste calls). Filing a `plan/PHASE_CANDIDATES.md` candidate for this so `/oversight` can decide which path to take; the two-line `always()` fix itself is ready to apply verbatim once either path is resolved.
> This exact diagnosis was filed as a Pending `plan/PHASE_CANDIDATES.md` candidate ([score 6.0], proposed 2026-07-05 by the nightly digest pass) — the fix is a low-risk, well-scoped one-line-per-step change that doesn't need `/oversight` phase promotion on its own merits, matching the precedent of `newsletter-gap-survey.mjs` and `og-coverage-check.mjs` shipping directly via `/iterate` — but it turns out to need `/oversight` anyway, for an unrelated reason: the cloud push credential can't write `.github/workflows/*` at all.

### [x] [seo] [5.6] Article JSON-LD `image` field carries a relative SVG path, invalid for Google Rich Results — addressed in 32a95d6
- category: seo
- filed: 2026-07-08 by cloud /iterate audit (fresh general-purpose sweep)
- impact: 7 (100% of published articles — `packages/seo/src/buildJsonLd.ts:52` emitted `input.heroImage` — a site-relative `.svg` path from frontmatter, e.g. `/hero-art/<slug>.svg` — directly as the Article schema's `image` field. Google's Article rich-result image requirement is an absolute URL in JPEG/PNG/WebP/GIF; SVG is rejected and a relative URL isn't valid schema.org input at all. Same class of bug already fixed for `og:image`/`twitter:image` — `apps/web/src/app/article/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx`'s own comment documents that fix — but the JSON-LD field was never migrated to the dynamic PNG route. Unaudited because `apps/e2e/tests/meta.spec.ts` only asserts `@type: 'Article'`, never the `image` field's shape, and the unit test fixture used an already-absolute `.jpg` URL, masking the real call site's SVG-frontmatter input)
- ease: 8 (one call-site edit reusing the already-shipped `opengraph-image.tsx` PNG route instead of raw `heroImage`; no schema/route change)
- score: 5.6 (impact × ease / 10)
- evidence: confirmed via local `next dev` — `<meta property="og:image">` resolves to `/article/<slug>/opengraph-image/og?<hash>` (a real rendered PNG, `curl` 200 `image/png`); confirmed the route serves without the cache-busting hash query too.
- action: `buildArticleJsonLd` now emits `image: \`${canonicalUrl(path)}/opengraph-image/og\`` (only when `heroImage` is set, preserving prior omit-when-null semantics) instead of the raw frontmatter path; updated `packages/seo/src/__tests__/buildJsonLd.test.ts` fixture/expectation to match.
> `pnpm verify` full gate green: typecheck, 591 web + 33 seo + other package unit tests, 159 script tests, data:validate (69 records), build, size (108.5 KB / 200 KB budget), 974/974 e2e. `pnpm deploy:check` green (dpl_3KbzEKVW, 98s to ready).

- impact: 6 (`SwitchQuiz.tsx`/`KeycapSetQuiz.tsx` `handleSelect` scheduled a bare `setTimeout(() => setStep(s => s + 1), 150)` on every click with no guard against re-entry. Two clicks landing on the same rendered question before the 150ms delay fires both schedule an advance, so `step` jumps by 2 — the skipped question's key stays absent from the `QuizAnswers` object fed into `recommendSwitch`/`recommendKeycapSet`, which silently scores that dimension as 0 for every candidate with no error or visible signal. Live, indexed features (`/quiz/switch`, `/quiz/keycap-set`); plausible trigger (accidental double-click, fast re-answer))
- ease: 7 (guard re-entry via a ref-backed pending timer, cleared and rescheduled on every click — same shape in both near-identical components; needed matching regression tests in both, plus fixing four e2e loops that turned out to be unknowingly relying on the race to advance through all 4 questions without waiting for each render)
- score: 4.2 (impact × ease / 10)
- action: `SwitchQuiz.tsx` and `KeycapSetQuiz.tsx` — added a `pendingAdvance` ref cleared before each new `setTimeout` schedule, so only the latest click per question survives. New regression tests in both components' test files (double-click-same-question, double-click-then-complete-quiz). Updated `apps/e2e/tests/quiz.spec.ts` (both start-over tests) and `apps/e2e/tests/parts.spec.ts` (both browse-all-parts tests) to wait for each question to render between clicks, matching the existing safe pattern already used by the "shows results" tests in the same file.

> **Resolved (2026-07-16):** Initial hypothesis was a data bug (score's sign should match direction) — disproven by checking `score === spark.at(-1)` across all 197 rows in `data/trends/*.json` (zero exceptions), which shows `score` is a current-level number, not a signed delta, so flipping it would have broken that invariant and misrepresented the real level. The actual bug was in the two `formatDelta()` implementations (`apps/web/src/lib/tracker/index.ts`, `apps/web/src/components/home/TrendingTile.tsx`), which took the +/- prefix from `score`'s own sign instead of the authoritative `direction` field. Fixed both to derive sign from `direction` and magnitude from `Math.abs(score)`; existing tests (which only covered already-consistent score/direction combos) were unaffected, and new regression tests cover the down/positive-score and up/negative-score cases in both files. `pnpm verify` full gate green: typecheck, unit tests (94 web test files + others), data:validate, build, size, 1028/1028 e2e.

- impact: 7 (same impact reasoning as the closed-out #524 partial fix: these are the two highest-traffic dynamic route families, and soft-404s risk Search Console flags/wasted crawl budget)
- ease: 6 (originally scored — the fix looked mechanical: convert `article/[slug]/not-found.tsx` and `tag/[slug]/not-found.tsx` from reading `headers()` server-side to `usePathname()` client-side, then add `dynamicParams = false`. Implemented and verified directly against a local `next build && next start`: confirmed this does NOT work. With `dynamicParams` at the default (`true`), unknown slugs render the segment's own `not-found.tsx` — "did you mean" suggestions intact — but HTTP status is 200 (the pre-existing soft-404). With `dynamicParams = false`, unknown slugs correctly 404 — confirmed via curl — but Next.js bypasses the segment's own `not-found.tsx` boundary entirely and falls back to the root `not-found.tsx` ("Lost in the layout."), losing the suggestions; this happens regardless of whether the not-found page reads the pathname server-side or client-side, because the routing-layer rejection happens before the segment boundary is considered at all. `apps/e2e/tests/polish.spec.ts`'s two "did you mean" tests caught this immediately when the change was verify-gated. The two properties (accurate 404 status, segment-level "did you mean" UX) are confirmed mutually exclusive for these two routes under the current Next.js version — same trade-off already accepted for `/vendor/[slug]`/`/newsletter/[slug]`/`/part/[kind]` in #524, but those routes had no "did you mean" feature to lose, so it was free there. Here it isn't — an autonomous ease score can't be assigned to "which regression do we prefer")
- score: 4.2 (impact × ease / 10, as originally computed before the ease reassessment above — carried forward for continuity with the closed issue, not a live autonomous priority)
- next: `/oversight` call on which is preferred: (a) keep the current soft-404 (200 status, working "did you mean" suggestions) — the status quo since #524; or (b) accept `dynamicParams = false` (real 404, but the not-found page falls back to generic root copy with no suggestions) — same trade-off already made for the other 4 entity routes. A third option — building the "did you mean" suggestions into the *root* `not-found.tsx` with route-aware behavior — wasn't scoped in this investigation and could be a future `/plan-a-phase` candidate if (b) is preferred but the UX loss is unacceptable.
- issue: #533 (opened, investigated same tick, closed not-planned — see issue comments for the full local-repro evidence trail)
> Filed same-tick as investigated: the fresh sweep's top finding (score 4.2) matched a standing follow-up gap from #524's partial resolution, was implemented, and failed its own e2e coverage (`polish.spec.ts`'s two "did you mean" assertions) on the first `pnpm verify` pass. Rather than iterate blindly against a gate that was correctly catching a real, structural regression, did a direct local repro (`next build && next start` + curl, both `dynamicParams` states) to confirm the constraint before reverting — this is a routing-layer limitation, not an implementation bug, so further iterate-tick attempts at "just read the pathname differently" would repeat this same dead end. All file changes reverted to a clean working tree; no commit shipped this line of investigation. Falls through to the next candidate finding for this tick.

- ease: 7 (scoped fix: merge the fix-commit and the audit-follow-up commit into a single push in the shipping skills' Step 6/7 — e.g. skills/iterate.md — so two rapid-fire pushes ~20s apart don't double-trigger the git-integration webhook; no Vercel-side access needed)

> **Resolved (2026-07-19):** `skills/iterate.md` (Step 5/6), `skills/ship-a-phase.md` (Step 10/11), `skills/ship-content.md` (Step 7d/8), and `skills/march.md` (Step 0.5's trend-snapshot flow) all had the same two-commit shape where the first commit pushed immediately and a trailing audit/DoD-tick commit pushed again seconds later. Each now stages its trailing commit locally and pushes once, after both commits exist — new Hard rules document the pattern in each skill (iterate.md §7.8, ship-a-phase.md §7.12, ship-content.md §5.8). `skills/ship-content.md`'s Step 3a early issue-number checkpoint was deliberately left alone — it's a resumability checkpoint spanning minutes of agent work (content-curator/brander), not a rapid-fire pair, so collapsing it into a later push would reintroduce the crash-recovery gap phase 24 built it to close. `pnpm verify` full gate green: typecheck, unit, data:validate (72 records), build, 1055/1055 e2e. ### [blocked-cloud-permission] [engineering] [4.0] heartbeat.yml wedged-run dedup search doesn't scope by workflow name — can silently suppress a distinct alarm
- category: engineering
- filed: 2026-07-26 by cloud /iterate audit (fresh general-purpose sweep, pass 241)
- impact: 5 (`.github/workflows/heartbeat.yml`'s "Cancel wedged runs" step loops over `march` and `night`; when a run is cancelled it checks for an existing open issue via `gh issue list --search "in:title \"Heartbeat: cancelled wedged run\" state:open"` before opening a new one — but that search string omits `$wf`, while the created issue's title embeds it (`"...cancelled wedged run ($wf, <timestamp>)"`). - category: engineering

- impact: 4 (`pnpm audit` reported 2 high-severity advisories, both js-yaml, both from GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj / CVE-2026-59870 published 2026-08-06 — quadratic-time `!!omap` resolution in both the 3.x and 4.x lines, never backported to 5.x. Root `package.json`'s `pnpm.overrides` — `js-yaml@<3.15.0: 3.15.0` and `js-yaml@>=4.0.0 <=4.1.1: 4.3.0` — were written for a prior advisory and now pin exactly to the two versions this new advisory flags (3.15.0, 4.3.0; patched are `>=3.15.1`, `>=4.3.1`).
